FileInfoListener handles both New/UpdatedFileInfoEvent but, when size bucket count>1, asks findBySize(size) with default onlyEmptyHash=true. Mapper restricts to file_hash IS NULL. Thus modified already-hashed files in a duplicate-size bucket are excluded from this recalculation path. updateFileMeta updates size/mimetype/owner/ignored but does not clear hash. Event registration confirmed NodeWritten/Touched -> filesystem save -> UpdatedFileInfoEvent -> same listener. No native end-to-end server reproduction.

NewHashListener hashA->hashB updates only B when newhash nonnull; oldA cleanup branch occurs only when currenthash null. Residual old duplicate record may remain until other cleanup; UI service filters groups to>1 currentlylinked files. No live database counterexample executed.

ScannerUtil checks interruption only after saveScannedFile, after caught NotFound/ForcedIgnore or completed save. No check before blocking scanner/hash operations and no latency bound. Other exceptions can escape scanner callback; FileInfoListener separately catches allThrowable and logs, without propagating incomplete scan status.

Shared-node filter uses strpos(nodepath,requestedpath)==0, a loose comparison rather than explicit===0 or component-aware ancestry. False and0 ambiguity and sibling-prefix boundary are source concerns, not a validated Nextcloud traversal reproduction.

FileDuplicateMapper orders id first and uses id>offset, so v1 ordering/cursor mismatch concern is not supported by the now-read implementation. Requestedhash/type ordering is secondary toid. Userargument unused in mapper, access filtering performed later in service.

FileInfoMapper.find matches sha1(path) plus optionalowner, without exactpath postcheck in method. SHA1 used intentionally as path index, not contenthash. Collision/admission implications not tested; no exploit or practical collision claim.
